project.name: ecommerce-clean-architecture
project.description: An ASP.NET Core e-commerce RESTful API implementing Clean Architecture principles, CQRS pattern with MediatR, FluentValidation, Entity Framework Core, and ASP.NET Core Identity with JWT authentication.
project.primary_purpose: Provide backend API services for managing an e-commerce platform including user identity, product catalogs, categories, shopping cart lifecycles, and orders.

actors.name: Anonymous User
actors.role: Public visitor with unauthenticated access to browse products, view categories, register accounts, authenticate (sign-in), and confirm email addresses.

actors.name: Authenticated Customer
actors.role: Registered customer authenticated via JWT Bearer tokens with authorization to manage shopping carts, add/remove cart items, checkout, and view order history.

actors.name: Administrator
actors.role: Privileged user role authorized to create, update, and delete products and categories, inspect user accounts, and retrieve top-selling sales analytics.

evidence.description: Main entry point and web application configuration written in C#
ASP.NET Core Web API project configuration
EF Core AppDbContext definition handling domain model mappings and database transactions
MediatR IPipelineBehavior implementation for request validation
FluentValidation integration for validating CQRS commands and queries
AutoMapper profile for domain entities to response DTO mappings
Container specification for building and deploying the e-commerce service
Multi-container orchestration definition for service runtime

core_components: API Layer (ecommerce.api): HTTP controllers exposing REST endpoints and routing requests
Application Layer (ecommerce.application): CQRS handlers, MediatR commands/queries, validation behaviors, and business services
Domain Layer (ecommerce.Domain): Core enterprise entities, aggregate roots, specification pattern interfaces, and enums
Infrastructure Layer (ecommerce.infra): EF Core AppDbContext, repositories, specification evaluators, Unit of Work, and JWT token services

global_middlewares.name: ExceptionMiddleware
global_middlewares.description: Catches unhandled application exceptions globally and maps them into consistent API error responses

global_middlewares.name: CorsMiddleware
global_middlewares.description: Configures Cross-Origin Resource Sharing policy based on application options

global_middlewares.name: Authentication & Authorization Middleware
global_middlewares.description: Validates JWT Bearer tokens and enforces role-based identity claims on protected endpoints

global_middlewares.name: ValidationBehavior
global_middlewares.description: MediatR pipeline behavior executing FluentValidation validators before dispatching commands and queries

architecture.data_flow_summary: Inbound HTTP requests hit ASP.NET Core Controllers in ecommerce.api -> Global ExceptionMiddleware intercepts errors -> Authenticated requests are verified via JWT Bearer middleware -> Controller dispatches Command/Query through MediatR pipeline -> ValidationBehavior runs FluentValidation -> CQRS Handler invokes Domain Specifications and Application/Infrastructure Services -> Repositories query database via EF Core AppDbContext -> Domain entities are mapped to DTO responses via AutoMapper -> ResponseHandler wraps results into standard JSON responses returned to client.
